questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

Inspite of the doctor's stern warning (1)/ Latika continued taking (2)/ sugars in her milk. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** 3

Sugar is an uncountable noun and therefore, does not have any plurals, i.e., ‘sugars’ is incorrect. The correct sentence is: 'In spite of the doctor’s stern warning, Latika continued taking sugar in her milk'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'. **

Myself and Roshni (1)/ will take care of (2)/ the event on Sunday. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **1

‘Myself’ is a reflexive pronoun, i.e., it needs something to refer to. Since the sentence does not have an ‘I’, using ‘myself’ is incorrect. The correct sentence is: 'Roshni and I will take care of the event on Sunday'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

_____ the rain stopped, the concert had to be suspended.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: Until

‘Until’ is used in situations where one event is dependent on another event. In this case, the ‘suspension’ was dependent on the ‘stopping of the rain’.

‘Unless’ is used in cases of exception, while ‘till’ can’t be used to begin a sentence. ‘While’ denotes continuity and changes the meaning of the sentence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

The elephant stampeded and tore _____ the streets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'** i.e. **'Down'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"down"** is the **appropriate preposition** to use with the verb **"tore" (past of "tear").**
 
• **"Tore down"** is a phrasal verb which **means** to destroy or remove something in a forceful and often reckless manner.
 
• The **sentence suggests** that the elephant was in a state of stampede and was destructively running through the streets.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'The elephant stampeded and tore **down** the streets.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's the explanation for the other options:
 
 
• **On -** "Tore on" doesn't make sense in this context. "On" could be used with verbs like "ran" or "rushed" ("The elephant ran on the streets"), but not with "tore".
 
• **Out -** "Tore out" typically means to remove something quickly or violently, often from a book or a piece of paper. It doesn't fit well with the action of an elephant running through the streets.
 
• **Off -** "Tore off" means to remove something quickly or violently, like tearing off a piece of cloth. It also doesn't fit well in this context.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Scuttle
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Brazier**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Scuttle"** means to run hurriedly or furtively with short quick steps. (तेज़ी से भागना)

 
 
• **Example: **The mouse scuttled across the floor, trying to avoid being seen.
 
 
 
• **"Brazier" **refers to a portable heater consisting of a pan or stand for holding lighted coals. (अंगीठी)
 
 
• **Example: **They gathered around the brazier to keep warm during the cold night.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Brazier**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Solitary **(अकेला): Existing alone; without companions.

 
 
• **Example:** He led a solitary life in the mountains.
 
 
 
• **Superficial **(ऊपरी): Existing or occurring at or on the surface.
 
 
• **Example: **Her injury was only superficial and didn't require stitches.
 
 
 
• **Soothing** (सुखदायक): Having a gently calming effect.
 
 
• **Example:** The soothing music helped her relax.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. **

Loquacious
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** Talkative

‘Loquacious’ means ‘tending to talk a great deal; talkative’. Therefore, the word ‘talkative’ has the same meaning and is the correct answer.

Foolishness denotes stupidity, graceful denotes elegance and entertainer is someone who entertains.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Obfuscate
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: Clarify

‘Obfuscate’ means ‘to make obscure or unclear; confuse’. ‘Clarify’, on the other hand, means ‘make less confusing and more comprehensible’. Hence, it is the correct answer.

Puzzle and haze both mean the same thing as obfuscate and envelop means to cover or surround completely.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Triumph
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Sorrow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Triumph"** means a great victory or achievement. (विजय)

 
 
• **Example: **His triumph in the marathon was celebrated by everyone in the town.
 
 
 
• **"Sorrow" **refers to a feeling of deep distress caused by loss, disappointment, or other misfortune suffered by oneself or others. (दुःख)
 
 
• **Example: **She was filled with sorrow after hearing about the untimely demise of her friend.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Triumph' **is **'Sorrow'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Sorrow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Establish **(स्थापित करना): To set up on a firm or permanent basis.

 
 
• **Example:** The company plans to establish a new branch in the city.
 
 
 
• **Disdain **(तिरस्कार): The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's consideration or respect.
 
 
• **Example: **He looked at the messy room with disdain.
 
 
 
• **Elation** (उल्लास): Great happiness and exhilaration.
 
 
• **Example:** The team felt a sense of elation after winning the championship.

questions.solution:

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

He jumped off the train while it (had been running).
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **was running

The correct answer is ‘was running’ since the sentence follows the past continuous tense, i.e., the action of ‘jump’ was performed while the train was in motion. The other options use the incorrect form of the verb.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

I (didn't see) him since we met two years ago.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** have not seen

‘Did not see’ implies that the activity of ‘seeing’ is completed and there is not further possibility of seeing, while ‘have not seen’ indicates continuity and the possibility that the situation might resolve. Therefore, the correct usage of ‘see’ is ‘have not seen’, due to the presence of ‘two years ago’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase. **

One who is new to a profession
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: Tyro

‘Tyro’ means a beginner or a novice, i.e., somebody who is new to something. Nuance means a subtle difference, pun is a play on words and a vandal is a person who deliberately destroys property.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase. **

A speech or a presentation made without previous preparation.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **Extempore

‘Extempore’ means spoken or done without preparation. Hence, it is the correct one-word substitute. Euphemism means a mild substitution, obituary means a notice of death and soliloquy is a monologue.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: And the victims are likely to be the poorest of the poor as well as the very sources of water- rivers, wetlands and aquifers.

Q: In India, water conflicts are likely to worsen before they begin to be resolved.

R: Till then they pose a significant threat to economic growth, security and health of the ecosystem.

S: Water is radically altering and affecting political boundaries all over world, between as well as within countries.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: SQPR

The sentences talk about water conflicts and the threats they pose. Therefore, the opening sentence of the passage must introduce the concept of water conflicts, which is done only by Sentence S. Moreover, Sentence P begins with an ‘and’, and cannot start a passage. Hence, the correct answer is SQPR.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: For one, very few entrepreneurs are willing to take on a new outsourcer, unless it comes with a guarantee of a certain level of sales.

Q: This invariably acts as an incentive for outsources to be lax in developing the business.

R: Despite being the dominant partner in the relationship, the outsourcer doesn't always have all the advantages.

S: The trade refers to it as the minimum guarantee clause, which means that if an outsource is unable to reach an anticipated sales level, he will be compensated for the balance amount.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **RPSQ

The sentences talk about sales and outsourcer. Therefore, the opening sentence of the passage must introduce the concept of ‘outsourcer’.

When reading Sentence S, it consists of an ‘it’, which refers to something else and can’t be the opening sentence.

Sentence Q uses ‘this’, which is a reference.

Sentence P uses ‘for one’, as a reason for something and has a reference.

Therefore, only Sentence R is free of references and is the opening sentence. Hence, the correct answer is RPSQ.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

Somebody told me that there had been a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.

options.text: I was informed that there was a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.
I was told by somebody that there had been a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.
I was told by somebody about a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.
I was told about a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** I was told by somebody that there had been a robbery in the jewellery exhibition.

Sentences 1 and 4 are incorrect because it is missing the speaker of the action, ‘somebody’, while Sentence 3 twists the meaning of the sentence and removes the information that the robbery was already conducted. Only Sentence 2 changes the active voice to the passive voice properly.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

Rohan said, "Where shall I be this time next month?"

options.text: Rohan contemplated where shall he be that time the following month.
Rohan asked that where should be that time next month.
Rohan wondered where he should be that time the next month.
Rohan wondered where he would be that time the following month.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: Rohan wondered where he would be that time the following month.

The sentence, in the indirect speech, should use only past-tense and third-person. Sentence 4 changes I to ‘he’, ‘this’ to ‘that and ‘next month’ to ‘following month’. Hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question: The modes of action are _____ in science and religion.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: different

The passage elaborates on the distinctions of science and religion. Therefore, the correct word to fill in the blank is ‘different’.

questions.question: whereas religion is based on experience. Any religious _____ whether
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **experience

The previous sentence used experience to define what religion is based on. Therefore, the correct word to fill in the blank here is ‘experience’. Moreover, the sentence talks about Christ or Ramakrishna, who had religious experiences that they shared with the world.

questions.question: it is Christ's or Ramakrishna's is personal and _____.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** subjective

‘Subjective’ means ‘based on feelings, experience and changes by the individual’. To say that religious experiences are subjective means that an experience differs from person to person and is not constant, which is true.

questions.question: Theory has to be corroborated by _____ proof providing material comforts.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: tangible

‘Tangible’ means ‘perceptible by touch’. The passage talks about science and religion. The sentence says that all theoretical proofs need to have some practical or physical proof as well. Hence, ‘tangible’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: The frontiers of science do not end in knowledge but are _____ to the formation of appliances for actual use.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: extended

‘Extended’ means ‘make larger or apply to’. The sentence says that science is not restricted only to knowledge, but is applied for actual use as well.
